Now, you see big versus small, as well, so try sticking with your lucky colors (remember yellow small gnome, brown big hat gnome).  Whenever a color that you've had good luck with pops up on screen, keep choosing that color.  When that gnome stops giving you points, or it drops down to fewer than 10 points, try the other color.  So if yellow stops working for you, try the red gnome.  Overall, the trick to this game to is remember where you've had good luck, and to try the other colors/hat sizes once that luck starts to run out.

text: The colors of the gnomes that lead you to more mushrooms varies. My best strategy would be: between colors A and B, first choose one at random. Say you chose A. Take note of whether it is relatively high or low. Then, those same colors are typically shown again (not always but usually!) This time, choose B and note if it is higher or lower than A. It is best to do this on a x1 round, in case B is a dud. And if A gave a very high number, and the round is x5, it may be better to just stick with it for now. Remember which color gave you better results. Stick with this color when it is an option, unless pitted against an entirely new color, C. It is best to choose C when the stakes are lower (x1), but it is important to find out how that color fares relatively quickly, before it changes. Continue to remember the high yield colors and choose those. Eventually, you will notice a color that you had success with now leads to far fewer mushrooms. At this point, start from scratch to find out what the new high yield colors are. Some other things I believe I discovered: size of hat, color of the basket, and which side the gnomes are on does not seem to make a difference. Of course, take this advice at your own risk. However, following this method led me to score roughly 4000 points for reference :) Best of luck!

parent_text: There are two colours of baskets in the game. Red, brown, pink and purple gnomes take you to a red basket, whereas green, blue, orange and yellow gnomes take you to the yellow basket. The points you earn is trial and error at first, but the gnomes will either be assigned to a 0-4 point bracket or 5-9 point bracket. You can tell which will score higher when the number of the mushrooms for that colour basket start to increase as you progress through the game. When the number of mushrooms being produced from the basket starts to drop, you know that you need to switch to a gnome that will take you to the opposing basket. Points can fluctuate between the two baskets so you need to make sure to keep switching between baskets depending on the number of mushrooms it is producing.
